TIG ROTATOR CONTROLS

150minutes
34solder joints
16screw clamps
difficulty

Low-voltage control wiring for the ESP32-P4 TIG welding rotator

Layout not verified for DM542T signal terminal, ESP32-P4 touch board (JP1). Measure the real part before printing the case.

Heat the pad and the pin together for two seconds. Feed solder into the joint, not onto the iron. Take the solder away first, then the iron.

Strip 3 mm, twist the strands, and tin the end before you solder it to a pad. Do not tin a wire that goes under a screw: a tinned end settles under the screw and works loose.

Unplug USB before you solder or change a wire. Work on a surface that does not burn, and wash your hands after handling solder.

Solder and clamp a yellow wireESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) GPIO50DM542T signal terminal PUL+

Step pulses to the driver

The end at the DM542T signal terminal PUL+ goes under a screw, not into solder: strip 5 mm, twist the strands tight or crimp on a ferrule, push the end fully in, tighten the screw and tug the wire to check it holds. Do not tin it.

27TIG-ROTATOR-CONTROLS-WIRE-1

Before you switch it on

  1. Look. Every joint is a shiny cone. No solder touches a neighbouring pad. No stray strands of wire. Tug every wire under a screw: none moves.
  2. These must not beep. Set the multimeter to continuity and probe each pair. A beep means a short: find it before you plug in.
    3V3GND3V3_2GND
  3. These must beep. Probe the two ends of every connection.
    STEPESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) GPIO50 · DM542T signal terminal PUL+
    DIRESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) GPIO51 · DM542T signal terminal DIR+
    ENAESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) GPIO52 · DM542T signal terminal ENA+
    DRIVER_ALMESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) GPIO32 · DM542T signal terminal ALM+
    GNDDM542T signal terminal PUL- · DM542T signal terminal DIR- · DM542T signal terminal ENA- · DM542T signal terminal ALM- · ESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) GND
    3V3ESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) 3V3 · Speed pot 3
    GNDSpeed pot 1 · ESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) GND_2 · Direction switch CW/CCW 1
    POTESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) GPIO49 · Speed pot 2
    DIR_SWITCHESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) GPIO29 · Direction switch CW/CCW COM
    3V3_2ESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) 3V3_2 · E-STOP interface input (3V3 / SIG / GND) 1 · Pedal ADC (ADS1115) VDD · Foot pedal socket 1
    ESTOPE-STOP interface input (3V3 / SIG / GND) 2 · ESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) GPIO34
    GNDE-STOP interface input (3V3 / SIG / GND) 3 · ESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) GND_3 · Pedal ADC (ADS1115) GND · Pedal ADC (ADS1115) ADDR · Foot pedal socket 3
    I2C_SDAESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) I2C_SDA · Pedal ADC (ADS1115) SDA
    I2C_SCLESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) I2C_SCL · Pedal ADC (ADS1115) SCL
    PEDAL_POTFoot pedal socket 2 · Pedal ADC (ADS1115) AIN0
    PEDAL_SWESP32-P4 touch board (JP1) GPIO33 · Foot pedal socket 4
  4. Plug in the USB cable. Nothing gets warm, nothing smells. If something does, unplug USB at once and check the wires against the table above.
  5. Flash the bring-up test. It reports every part it can find before you load the real firmware.pio run -e bringup -t upload && pio device monitor
28TIG-ROTATOR-CONTROLS-WIRE-1

TIG Rotator Controls is built

The low-voltage controller subsystem of the DIY TIG welding positioner: the GUITION JC4880P443C ESP32-P4 touch board, its speed pot, direction switch, foot pedal (switch plus ADS1115 pot), conditioned E-STOP input and the DM542T signal terminal. Motor power, the stepper, gearbox and the grounded metal enclosure are outside this package.
